stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A plane wave in a ripple tank crosses the boundary between two zones of different celerities. The source period $T = 50\,\text{ms}$ is fixed, so $\lambda = c\,T$. Sweep celerities $c_1$, $c_2$ and incidence angle $i_1$ to see how the refracted wave bends and how its wavelength changes.
stages.concept: Snell's law for waves: $\dfrac{\sin i_1}{\sin i_2} = \dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}$. Slower zone $\Rightarrow$ smaller angle from the normal AND shorter wavelength. Frequency is preserved across the interface.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target refracted angle $i_2^{*}$ and target refracted wavelength $\lambda_2^{*}$ are shown at the interface. Tune $c_1$, $c_2$, $i_1$ until the refracted wavefronts align with both target markers. Many triples work — only the ratios matter.
stages.concept: $\lambda_2^{*} = c_2\,T\ \Rightarrow\ c_2 = \lambda_2^{*}/T$ pins $c_2$. Then $\sin i_2^{*} = \dfrac{c_2}{c_1}\,\sin i_1$ leaves $(c_1, i_1)$ constrained on one curve — pick any convenient $c_1$ and solve for $i_1$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The refracted wavefronts are hidden. Only the incident wave, the interface, and the target markers $i_2^{*}$ and $\lambda_2^{*}$ remain. Compute $c_1$, $c_2$, $i_1$ on paper, set the sliders, then submit. One shot per setup.
stages.concept: From $\lambda_2^{*}$: $c_2 = \lambda_2^{*}/T$. From $i_2^{*}$: $\sin i_1 = \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\,\sin i_2^{*}$. Fix a convenient $c_1$ (say, the midpoint), then $i_1 = \arcsin\!\left(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\,\sin i_2^{*}\right)$.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider to at least half its range
labels.tip2: align the refracted wave with both target markers
labels.tip3: compute c1, c2, i1 on paper, then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: λ₂* = c₂·T pins c₂. Then sin(i₁) = (c₁/c₂)·sin(i₂*). Pick c₁, solve for i₁.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: T = 50 ms. If λ₂* = 10 mm, then c₂ = 0.20 m/s. Every 5 mm of λ₂ = 0.10 m/s of c.

1.1: Which slider changes the refracted angle most? Try holding two fixed and moving the third.
1.2: λ₁ = c₁·T. Watch the spacing of the incident wavefronts as you slide c₁.
1.3: When c₂ < c₁, i₂ < i₁ (wave bends toward the normal). Reverse if c₂ > c₁.

2.1: The refracted wavelength target λ₂* depends only on c₂. Start there.
2.2: With c₂ fixed, the ratio sin(i₁)/sin(i₂*) = c₁/c₂ leaves one degree of freedom.
2.3: Fix c₁ at 0.30 m/s. Then i₁ = arcsin((c₁/c₂)·sin(i₂*)) is a direct calculation.

3.1: The refracted wave is hidden but the formulas still hold. Write them on paper first.
3.2: Step 1: c₂ = λ₂*/T. Step 2: pick any c₁ in range. Step 3: i₁ = arcsin((c₁/c₂)·sin(i₂*)).
3.3: Peek reveals the inverse formula. Apply it to the numeric target shown at the interface.
